finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-chosen URL that is only checked with a substring match, so the server can be made to request internal hosts (e.g. loopback or cloud metadata), and redirects are followed to further targets.
finding.source: main.go:31 r.FormValue("logo") (query string or form body, fully attacker-controlled)
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw) with the default client, which follows up to 10 redirects

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo"); attacker supplies any URL
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only check; it matches anywhere in the string, including path, query, fragment, or userinfo
http.Get(raw) uses the original string, not a parsed/validated URL; scheme, host, port, and IP are never checked
Default client follows redirects, so an allowed-looking origin can 30x to http://127.0.0.1/... or http://169.254.169.254/..., which the substring check never sees
io.Copy streams the response body back to the caller, so the SSRF is readable (not blind)

finding.guards_checked: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at line 32. Not present: url.Parse, https-only scheme allow-list, exact hostname allow-list, port restriction, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, dial-time or DNS-pinning check, CheckRedirect/redirect restriction. Example payloads: logo=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/x#example.io (fragment is not sent but satisfies the check); logo=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io; logo=http://attacker.example/redir?example.io where the attacker's server 302s to an internal address.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, which is a substring match and does not close the finding. No url.Parse, scheme allow-list, hostname membership, IP blocking, or CheckRedirect exists on the /logo path (main.go:30-39). The noRedirect/trusted-host protections at main.go:10-12 and 20-24 apply only to the /cdn handler.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-supplied "logo" parameter unauthenticated, main.go:32 only checks that "example.io" appears anywhere in the string, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with DefaultClient, which follows redirects and returns the body via io.Copy at main.go:38, so the SSRF is readable.
